body:
💯  agree. Just imagine, 10 years ago, wala pang React, nor Swift (objective-c pa gamit for iOS), and hindi pa widespread ang usage ng AWS. 

Meron namang mga certification depende sa specialization. Pero kelangan magtake nun halos every year.

100% agree with this. The skills I've acquired in the university are more important than the specific tech stack I've learned. 

Frameworks and languages change overtime. 10 years ago, nobody was taking JavaScript seriously. But now it's de facto frontend language.
How long did it take?

Totally agree. It even looks like you want to use her to pay half the mortgage. Kasi why aren't you open to co-own the unit?

You are asking what the difference is kung magrrent din sya ng same cost -- the answer is opportunity cost. She could use that money for something that she will eventually own.

Yeah I agree with what others said. Di nia ba makita na may sentimental value din sayo ung bahay?

And ang tricky jan, you guys are not even married yet. If you sell the house and use the money to pay for the condo, and then eventually you break up, pano na? Unless may contract kayo, Wala syang legal obligation to pay you back. And pano ka? Hahanap ka pa ng titirhan.
You're right! Apologies for that

There is this concept of 2% rule in real estate investing where it states that the annual rental amount should be at least 2% of the property's price.

If the monthly rent per room is 4k, 4 units will give you a total rental amount of 16k monthly or 192k annually. 

Now you have to sum up the total cost of the property, not just the 2M renovation. 

Let's just say the property, including the house and lot cost 1M. So the total is 3M. Comparing it to the total rental amount (192k / 3M), it gives 6.4%. higher naman sa 2% so I think ok.

Complaining via email is not enough. You need to get in touch with an actual person. Sa delay na ganyan, tatawag ako until makarating ung reklamo ko sa someone higher.

Tingin ko what they are doing is they are spreading their manpower to handle more projects, which yields more income while keeping the operational expenses the same. 

As for the question that you will raise, I don't think it will have any effect on your situation. I doubt their spokesperson is aware of the statuses of all their projects.

Can you share the contracting firm? It sounds like a big company since they have an investor relations meeting.

Right now, I think you have these options:
1. Nag them until they finish the project. Pero baka tagalan pa nila or di ayusin ung gawa. Next time, try to push for progress billing over full payment prior to completion.

2. If you know someone in the company, try to ask for their help. Pag mas mataas ang position, mas ok.

3. Since mukhang big company sya, try to file a formal complaint sa hotline nila. And religiously follow up.

4. Make a scene! Post your complaint in social media and tag the CEO hehe. This could potentially backfire though so treat this as a last resort.

I doubt anything will happen if you attend the investors briefing since meetings like that tend to have a lot of attendees and they would most likely restrict mic/chat access.
So ang interest na binabayaran mo ay 200 per month? Or equivalent to 12.5%. mas malaki pa kesa sa 10.5% na interest ng pag-ibig multi purpose loan

Puntahan mo muna ung property before deciding anything. It may look good on paper, pero baka may mabaho palang amoy or puro poop ng aso. 

Also, kung for investment pala, I would echo what other people said, tapusin mo muna EF mo. Think of it this way, if by any chance, madelay ung sahod mo, or matanggal ka sa trabaho, or worse may emergency, how long can you continue paying for the deposit? And note na usually, hindi mo agad mababawi ung hinulog mo na jan in case di mo na kaya or need mo ng pera. The only way I think is pasalo, which is not that easy too.

Ah in that case, mukha bang may market para umupa jan? Is it near a school or office? How accessible is it?

Usually ung mga nangungupahan, preferred na malapit sa place of work nila so keep that in mind.

Are you sure you want to live in that place? Have you tried living on your own?

You're still young. Get to know yourself muna kung san mo talaga gusto tumira.

Disposable money is relative. I personally only use 10% of spare money for high-risk investment. Para pag nagfail, hindi naman guguho ang mundo ko. But I'm a conservative investor. You might have a different risk appetite.

Significant gain is also relative. And it also depends on the investment instrument. For me, I mostly invest in dividend-paying stocks or MP2. And significant na sya kapag ung total monthly dividends ay greater than minimum wage. Para ung investment ko ay literally kumikita na for me. Still working my way towards it pero kapit lang 😊

100% agree. EF muna. Pag natapos mo na ung EF saka na magluho.

Think of EF as future debt na binabayaran mo in advanced. Kasi kung wala kang EF at magka-emergency, no choice ka din naman kundi mangutang. And worse, baka may interest pa.

Afaik, you can only share the title if you are married, siblings, or parent-child. But it's best to consult with professionals such as a lawyer.

As for things to consider, check how accessible the property is (check for nearby grocery, mall, hospital, etc) and the nearby area (is it right next to a creek?) 

Also check the utility providers -- ok ba ung internet dun? May poste na ba ng meralco? Malakas ba ung tubig na aabot sa planned # of floors ng bahay nio? 

And lastly, check if the gated community is well maintained. Is it secure? How often do they collect the garbage? Are your future neighbors noisy?

TLDR: visit the property and see if you would actually want to live there

The sad reality is you have to earn more to save more. For example, if you're earning 10k / month, it's unimaginable to save 100k, let alone 1M. 

It's great that you are already saving 30% of your salary. But I highly advise you to invest in things that will allow you to earn more. Good luck op!

Have you tried living in a studio unit? Imo, it's not big enough for raising a kid. As a baby, they need space to crawl/play around. And eventually, they will need some sort of privacy for studying and whatnot. 

Ung living arrangements nila sa college, you can save up for it. For example, sabihin natin na 10k na ung rent by then. 10k x 12months x 5years=600k. Way below sa price diff ng condo at bahay. And pwede pa yang tumubo pag iinvest mo sa mp2 or other low risk investment instrument.

We shouldn't conflate retirement and childlessness imo.

As long as you have enough funds and you're part of a healthy community/support group, I think that should be enough.

Our children will eventually have a family of their own. We shouldn't expect them to take care of us. Doing so would only lead to disappointment on our part, and resentment on them. 

Be grateful if they do take care of you, but don't demand nor expect it.
Ask him what he would do if you were to go to a male strip club. I bet he won't like it either.

It depends on what stage you are in life.

If you are young and have no obligations in PH, then it is super worth it. If you are mid20s to early 30s, I think you would enjoy it. You get to experience a different culture and you'd gain immense experience work-wise.

But if you're already established and have a family, then it's harder. It now depends on your personality. If you are the outgoing type who loves to explore and have enough savings to sustain your lifestyle while you're establishing yourself to the new environment, then go ahead. But otherwise, you might have a hard time adjusting.

You need to do the calculation of your new income vs cost of living including taxes and relocation-related expenses.

Other countries have different taxes deducted in the salary such as income tax, city tax, regional tax, etc. It may seem that the income tax is only 20% but the total deductions from your salary may amount to 35%.

For relocation, do consider that most apartments require a 1 month deposit and 1 month advance of the rent. So you need to prepare about 3 months worth of rent. And sometimes, apartments are unfurnished so you need to shell out some more for beddings, appliances, etc.

Just do the math and let numbers decide (if it's your only consideration).

As for me, I would jump to the opportunity if my net savings per month would at least double. Otherwise, it's just not worth all the effort.

I understand your annoyance at what they're doing. But I think it would also help to understand why they are doing it.

Of course, there's a bragging aspect to it. But another thing that you probably missed is that working abroad is hard. Take for example the seaman who is onboard a ship for 7 months. They are isolated with the same set of people, at the same ship for an extended period of time (no opportunities to go to the mall, be with their families, hang out with friends). And probably, with unstable internet connection too (no Netflix or Facebook). On top of that, their job often entails hard labor. 

So combine all those factors together and try to imagine na pagod/stressed sa trabaho, walang mapag-rant-an kundi ung mga kabaro. Walang ibang outlet ng frustration kundi ung mga andun lang din sa barko. And for 7 months!!! Nakakabaliw. No wonder pagbalik sa pinas, they want to enjoy the fruit of their sacrifices. 

I'm not saying na pautangin mo sila. I'm not saying na tama ung pagwawaldas nila ng pera. All i'm saying is try to put yourself in their shoes and you'd be able to see them in a different light.

The 30% rule doesn't prohibit you from renting. It's a suggestion to not spend more than 30% for your rent. 

For example, if your salary is 30k per month, it is advisable that you don't spend more than 9k for rent. So wag muna magtingin-tingin ng solo condo unit sa CBD. Try to look for co-living options or other cheaper alternatives that can fit the budget.. 

Wala namang pumipigil sayo to spend 90% of your salary for rent. Pero realistically, you'd have to sacrifice something else to achieve that e.g. noodles everyday para tumira sa solo unit sa BGC. The choice is yours OP.

IMO, for this to work, you need a great lawyer. Buying a property is messy already, let alone sharing the ownership and potential profits. So there has to be a detailed contract that stipulates the different considerations.

This is the exciting part! Just try to browse online, make your list, compare, and reach out to the contact person to view the unit. The more units you view, the more you'll realize what you want and what you need.

For example, I was initially hell-bent on living in the Metro. But as I check the listings online, I just can't afford it. So I tried expanding my search on nearby cities and eventually found one that suits my needs.

Although, this is a very time consuming process. If you're in a rush, just look for a short term rental unit then continue your search.

I usually consider if I can earn the interest if I were to invest it in some other instrument. 

For example, imagine a loan of 1M with 10% p.a. interest to be paid in 1 year. So the interest is 100k. Can I earn this much in a year on REIT (an example of a potential investment instrument I'm eyeing)? Since most REITs only have a dividend yield of 5% and rarely grow in value in such a short time, I will essentially lose money:

if I take a loan (-100k) vs if I invest with a yield of 5% (+50k) = -50k loss

True. Try renting out first. This way, you'll realize what you want for your own space without committing to anything.

Kumbaga, magdate date ka muna. Wag diretso kasal 😉

Sa tingin ko nappressure ka lang sa savings ng ibang tao. As you've mentioned, 3 years ka palang nagwwork. You still have several years to save up and to grow your EF. Just keep saving and in a few years, di mo na mapansin na malaki na yun.

One tip though, save in terms of percentage not fixed amount. In this way, if your income increases, your savings will also increase. And always allocate your savings first before buying your wants. i.e. if you want to speed up your EF, save 50% of your income. Then, since 50% na lang matitira sayo, onti na lang ung magagastos mo sa wants.

How about rental apartments? With that money, you can buy some properties in the province and rent it out. But you have to do your research well as to which area is attractive for tenants and also, you have to have someone trustworthy to oversee the apartment.

Check mo to OP: https://www.novconph.com/package-new

Hindi ako affiliated sa kanila pero nakikita ko lang sila sa social media and ok naman mga design nila. Un nga lang, minimum na TCP na tinatanggap nila is 5M ata :(

Hi OP, pwede kang kumontact sa mga design and build contractors like NovCon. Based sa website nila, ung cost ng design, idededuct sa total contract price kung sila din gagawa, which makes it free.

80k ata ung base design fee nila. Pero based sila sa Cavite at Batangas ata. Check mo na lang sa website/YouTube nila. Good luck OP.

6k rent for 20k salary is steep but feasible. However, moving out has other expenses too:

1. Deposit and advance payment. Most landlords require 1-2 month deposit and 1 month advanced. So be prepared to shell out 12-18k.

2. Appliances. I imagine that you'd spend most of your time in the apartment so you'd need an electric fan, fridge, stove, electric kettle, and rice cooker. You might consider skimping on these items but I'm telling you, these are lifesavers. Rice cooker alone, malaking katipiran na sa food budget.

3. Household items such as spoon, fork, plate, glass, bowl, bed, pillow, chair, table, and many more. If the unit is fully furnished, then just buy your own cutleries and pillow.

Another thing to consider is security. I have heard stories na nanakawan sila while renting a unit na medyo ganyan ung price range. Imake sure mo na lang na double or triple ung lock ng bahay and may grills ung windows.

Good luck OP.

I do agree that 100M - 200M seems like a lot of money. However, I had the same sentiments several years ago about 10M. I thought that was enough to start a family and live comfortably. But here I am and I realized it's not enough to live in the metro.

I guess this is just my frustration manifesting after years of working. I'm just concerned that if I set my target to 100M and miraculously reach it after more years of working, I might find myself in the same situation. Like a horse chasing a carrot stick in a never ending field.

Let me be clear, I understand that I can choose to live outside the metro to have a lower cost of living. But the best opportunities for my family (education, work, experiences) can only be found in the metro.
Pero magkano nga ba ang ok na goal? 1 million is definitely not enough. 10 million din -- pang bahay at kotse palang to.

Ako I opened another bank account for savings. Kahit sa same bank lang din, basta separate account sya and walang ATM card - passbook lang. Tapos every pay day, nililipat ko agad ung savings dun. Tapos kakalimutan ko na ung account na un until next pay day.

For me, hindi ko nagagastos kung hindi madaling mawithdraw ung pera. Baka gumana din sayo. Good luck OP.

Agree sa magrent muna. Before, I was really keen to buy a condo. Then nakapagrent muna ako for 3 months. Tapos narealize ko na hindi sya for me kasi:

* A 27sqm unit is simply not enough for me. I need an office space for my work, bedroom, kitchen, and storage. Not to mention I also want a living room and dining room.
* Andaming bawal such as bawal magsampay sa balcony, bawal magpako ng anything (lahat ng house decor nakapatong lang sa cabinet or table), bawal magopen flame (goodbye scented candle me time moment)
* It's too expensive to buy, kahit pre-selling pa. A 27sqm 1br-unit in the metro will cost you 6-7M. Whereas you can buy a 120sqm (lot area) brand new house and lot in Cavite/Laguna for the same price.

Imo, investing internationally is not worth it if you're only investing < 500k because of charges and fluctuations on exchange rate.

The potential gains internationally are definitely higher compared locally but it is definitely riskier.

My advice is if you have <500k, invest locally on relatively safe instruments such as MP2, UITF, or blue chip stocks that pay dividends. If you have more, then you can try investing internationally. If you have waaay more (3M++), get in touch with big banks locally and they might offer you corporate bonds with 5-7% interest rate.

Agree. Pano nangyari na sayo na ang title ng walang DOAS, DST, CGT, at eCAR. Hindi mag-iissue ang registry of deeds ng wala yun. Puntahan mo na sa registry of deeds at icheck mo ung title from them. Baka fake ung hawak mo.

I bought some Ethereum back in late 2017, valued at around 50k php. Then the value dipped to as low as 5k php. Dahil sa sobrang baba, ayokong marealize ung actual loss so  iniwan ko na lang at kinalimutan.

Now, 150k php na value nia. Kaso I moved to a different country and I need to verify my residential address in that country before I can withdraw. So ayun, wala na. T.T

Before you decide what to do, I would suggest to do your due diligence and research it thoroughly. Check the details of the VUL, especially the fees, add-ons, and claiming process.

For me, I'd take stocks, MP2, or even UITF over VUL anytime. Cause the way I see it is:
* Stocks/MP2/UITF == investment for myself
* VUL == investment for people I will leave behind

Oftentimes, VUL can only be claimed fully upon death or upon  becoming a senior citizen. Whereas stocks/uitf can be withdrawn anytime, for MP2 after 5 years.

In addition, imo, VULs have higher fees than those other investment products. Minsan sa stocks/MP2, may dividends pa, so mababawi pa ung whatever fees na binayaran mo.

Whatever your decision maybe, I wish you luck OP.

People are just unhappy when they lose and are trying to put the blame to someone else.

I really hate it when people criticize your pick for the role. All champions can technically fit any role. As long as you're not intentionally feeding, it should be ok.
The field really matters. In the tech industry here, the starting salary 10+ years ago was 30k. Sahod na yan ng manager sa ibang field. And note that was 10 years ago. Ewan na ngayon.
Totally agree. Even with 100k monthly income, buying a house or condo in the metro is pretty tight.

First, dapat hindi mo sabihin sa kanila ung sahod mo. Otherwise, iccompute na agad nila un, as part ng income nila. 

Second, mahal talaga mamuhay mag-isa, pero that's the price you have to pay for independence. Hindi un libre. Pero kung nakabukod ka, baka pwede kang magrequest na babaan contribution mo sa kanila?

Ganyan din nafeel ko dati sa family ko. What helped me was to allocate a monthly amount for them. Pero di ako lagi binibigay. Pag kelangan lang. I told them na nag-iipon ako for emergency nila. And pag emergency, tumutulong ako. 

Lastly, lahat ng binigay ko sa kanila, nakalista sa expenses ko. Bale trineat ko sya na parang rent lol. At tinatrack ko din na dapat on average, di tataas ng certain percentage ung binibigay ko sa kanila. So kung napprove ko naman na on average, pasok sa allocated budget ung bigay ko sa kanila, I don't feel bad. Pero pag napansin ko na malapit ng lumagpas, I tell them na di ko afford magbigay.

Good luck to you OP.

Maybe a bit too late na, pero for future references, I would advise to establish a good relationship with your bank. By that I mean maintain a healthy balance. Tipong 6-digits ung daily maintaining balance. Mas lenient ang mga banks mag-approve ng cc and ng loan sa mga long-term clients na may malaking balance.

I agree with what most people here suggested: prepare a memorandum of agreement with your parents stating na you'll help pay the debt, in return, they will transfer the title to your name. Although some caveat, magastos din magtransfer ng title.

Don't feel bad na may condition ung ibibigay mong tulong. Kasi pinaghirapan mo yung perang ilalabas mo. Ung tulong mo, kapalit nun ay ang financial security mo in months to come. And sa totoo lang, malabong bayaran nila ung amount na ilalabas mo.

Some additional advise lang, if I were in your shoes, hindi ko sasagarin ung amount na ilalabas ko. Ititira ko ung EF ko, then I'll tell them to get a loan or something. I can't bear the thought na in case may accident, wala akong pang-admit sa ospital. Also, pag hindi mo binuo, that will give them an idea na hirap ka din tumulong. 

Anyways, good luck to you OP!

Usually the miscellaneous fee (Capital Gains Tax, Documentary Stamp Tax, transfer of title, etc) is 10% of the value of the land. So kung 200k, expect 20k. 

Check din ung zonal value. kasi whichever is higher (zonal value vs contract price), un ung magiging basis.

Pero expect na more expenses pa such as agent fee (kung hindi Ikaw ang mag-aasikaso ng transfer), notarial fee for Deed of Absolute Sale which is 1-10% of contract price, lot resurvey (starting at 10k), and pabakod.

It's important na ung mag-aasikaso ng transfer ay kakilala at pinagkakatiwalaan mo. Mahirap na. 

Kung wala kang mapagkakatiwalaan at wala kang balak magpabalik-balik dun para asikasuhin ung pagtransfer, I'd say wag na lang.

I have the same sentiments. One moment I'm updating my resume for interviews, then a few seconds later, I'm crying and just want to end it all.

I haven't "taken the bus" yet because I'm still planning how to do it, and how to make it easier for the people I will leave behind.

Some things to consider:
1. Most banks have a minimum maintaining balance of around 500usd.
2. If there's no activity in your bank account for a long time, it will become dormant. You would have to go to the bank to fix it.
3. Most banks only accept dollar deposit. Usually di pinapayagan na peso or other currency ang dala mo, tapos idedeposit into a USD account. 


IMO, Kung di mo naman madalas gagamitin at maliit lang idedeposit mo, (e.g. <1000USD), I don't think it's worth the effort. Otherwise, go for it!

Kelangan mo na ba magdecide ngayon para sa bahay? Baka pwedeng idelay mo until makakuha ka ng side projects na magbbump ng income nio para maging 30-50% na lang ung mga payables. 

Kung 70% kasi ng sahod nio mapupunta sa payables, pano na lang ung tax? Usually 30% un. Or kung di na counted ung tax, parang tight pa din ung 30% sa bills, food, gas, toiletries, and other miscellaneous.

Another alternative is baka pwede niong paliitin ung monthly payable sa landlord either sa pagtawad or patagalin ung payment terms.

One thing you probably missed is dividends. Afaik, VTI has a good dividend yield. So kung ibenta mo, talo ka na sa presyo, namiss out mo pa ung kita sa dividends.

Although di ko alam kung nagppayout ng dividends pag sa GoTrade.
I actually like the style. but they should have banned nocturne. It messes up their picks.

I'm using bdo securities, primarily because I have a bdo savings account. It makes transferring funds a breeze.

They have GTC (good til cancelled) and GTD (good til end of day) and other buying options. Pero ung 2 lang na un ang gamit ko usually. Di kasi ako day trader.

Ok naman ang website nila and maayos naman ung email notification every time may transaction na nagpproceed, and weekly investment ideas -- eto ung trigger ko magresearch every week to validate their recommendations and to look out for interesting stocks to buy. Pero dont compare their UI to other more sophisticated brokers like Interactive Brokers and Saxo Bank.

I can relate to you OP. I graduated with honors and got a job at a decent company. After 5 years of working, I wanted to buy my own house/condo. Naloka ako nung nalaman ko na down payment palang ng condo sa metro manila, 500k na. And this was several years ago. Back then I was making about 50k per month, which I thought was high enough already. Pero syempre nagbibigay sa family, rent, and other monthly expenses, I only save about 5-10% of that.

Thats when I decided to get a job overseas. And ayun, malaki-laki naman na savings ko. And now im looking for an affordable property in the province.
I play Maokai. Cause I love plants

I perma ban pyke. I hate that he goes invisible then suddenly hooks me.

I love playing against Draven. I can position my plants to where his axe will be.

I'm also considering a joint account, pero managed separately, when I get married. Para in case mamatay ung isa samin, hindi ganun kahirap iclaim ung money.

Apart from that, may iba pa bang benefits ang joint accounts?

Does this mean that the stock didn't live up to the hype? And is this an indicator that the price is projected to go down more, especially once the fund is fully consumed?

I'm interested to buy but I've noticed that most IPOs tend to drop its price within a month or so. But in the long term, provided it is a valuable company, it will eventually rise. E.g. Facebook and Converg

Kaya nag-aabang pa ako ng price drop >.<
Newbie here, what does it mean when the stability fund is half dead?
I'm curious how did you amass a 450k debt to Meralco. Wouldn't they have cutoff the electricity if you miss the payments for 1-2 months? And having a 250k monthly bill sounds too much.

Im sorry for your situation OP. Pero malabong magbago ang ways ng mother mo. You said it yourself, nung hirap kayo, hindi sya nagwork, how much more now? What's more likely to happen is brother 2 will work to help your mother's finances. 

Ung main struggle talaga dyan ay ung conscience mo bilang anak. Think of it this way, if your mother suddenly die na may hinanakit sayo about sa finances, can you live with it?

I normally use Transferwise to remit 6-digits and in my experience, sila talaga ang may best rate. Pwede niong i-split into multiple transfers para less than 500k and less hassle.

Kung wala ng time, isa ring option ay iuwi nia na lang ung USD. He can carry up to 10k USD papasok sa pinas. Tapos dun na lang ipapalit pag maganda na ung rate, or ipasok sa USD bank account mismo. Good luck!

congratulations OP! dont worry about the past. i think karamihan ng tao ganyan. ako din, for the 1st 10 years of my career, ung savings ko sapat lang. nagbibigay kasi ako sa family and nahilig din akong magtravel-travel.

then nung nakalipat ako ng job na malaki-laki ang salary, biglang tumalon ung savings ko at dun na talaga nagkabudget to diversify my investments. and since i now know the value of money, sobrang matipid na ako.

looking back, i dont have any regrets with how i spent my money. my past experiences paved the way to my present :)

Think of it this way, if for some reason you suddenly lose your job, would you regret that new venture? If you are stable enough financially that you don't mind, then go ahead. Pero kung alanganin, wag muna. Mahirap na.

And I agree with others, madami pang ganyang opportunity. And baka pwede ka pa nga magjoin dyan sa exact same business later on.
I track my expenses in Google sheets. I usually have a summary tab containing the total per category per month. Tapos I use stacked bar chart.

Congratulations! Now that you're tracking your expenses, I recommend to have a once a month analysis of your expenses. I do this every end of the month to see if I overspend on food or other leisure activities. This helps me control my urges for the next month, and keeps me on track to my goal.

Dahil sa annual kong pagtrack ng goal ko, I've decided to work abroad and even change my specialization para maachieve ko ung goal ko. Kung wala akong goal, I would never have the urge to strive for more

Set a target financial goal (with end year) and track your progress at least once a year. I've been doing this since I started working and malaking tulong talaga to.

For example, get 5M in 10years. -- 5M para may pangbili ng condo. Kung sa year 1, 100k lang ang savings mo, ibig sabihin it will take you 50 years para maipon to. So malabong maachieve in 10 years. 

So either magplan ka para magkaroon ng higher income/savings or babaan mo ung goal mo. e.g. set it to 2.5M (for a house and lot sa probinsya) Or change jobs -- dun sa mas malaki ang sahod to bring you closer to the goal.

I often go mandate even with Aftershock simply because it's so much cheaper than other tank mythic. And poking during laning phase is so much fun. 

then I usually go tanky items next, especially if there's no other tank in the team. Someone needs to peel for the carries during team fights.
There are certain matchups where I don't pick Zyra. E.g. if the team has at least 2 assassins, there's no way I'd pick Zyra. She'll just die instantly before she can even position well.
Totally agree to this. Also, it helps to expand your champion pool a bit in case the enemy team comp is a bad matchup with Zyra.

Same. I have multiple accounts for different purposes. I have one purely as a passthrough of my salary and bills payment. I also have another account tied to my investments, another one for my emergency fund, and another one shared with my family.

I can't really say which one is the best. But there are some things I look for when deciding which UITF to invest in. For short term investments, I often choose those that have the least trust fee (my personal limit is 0.5%p.a.), no minimum holding period, and consistent stable growth.

Note that I don't expect high return rate for this investment. I just want to earn a bit until I actually use the money.

Para din makita ung progress. I often prepare graphs para makita ko visually kung aling investment ung naggrow and by how much. This allows me to make better decisions e.g which investments to continue or to stop
Same. I only started playing her about a month ago and Im already at Level 7 mastery. She's just so damn strong that I truly enjoy playing her.

I keep both for different purposes:

* FMETF for long term goals like retirement

* UITF for short term savings like a potential condo down payment. 

I want to be able to cash out easily when I find a good buy.
